claims.finding: On 2026-09-01, two days before the results print, Amber International announced it was abandoning its 'Amber Premium' digital-asset wealth identity and rebranding to AMBR as an 'agentic AI company', launching AI agents Ambre and MIA - a total repositioning of the business released at 3:30 AM ET on PR Newswire, immediately ahead of the numbers.

claims.why_not_priced: The headline is priced - it is what moved the stock. What is not priced is the read-through: a sub-$100m issuer that discards its entire brand and stated business model 48 hours before releasing results is almost always pre-framing a bad set of numbers, and there is no sell-side coverage, no news-search coverage (every snapshot has n_queries=0) and no analyst preview anywhere in this capture to make that connection. If the market had connected them, the pivot day would not have opened +14% pre-market on retail gapper lists.
claims.independence: The 6-K accepted 2026-08-31T09:21:07Z, three days before the print, is a second, company-sourced document pointing at unusual pre-print disclosure activity - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1697818/000110465926103605/tm2624351d1_6k.htm

claims.finding: quote.json shows 15,889,900 shares traded on 2026-09-01 against a 20-day average near 1.09m and a late-August run of 19k-55k a day - roughly 29% of the ~55m float turning over in one session, with the close at 0.88 after an intraday high well above 1.40, i.e. a complete distribution of the pivot rally into the print.
claims.why_not_priced: A 300x volume day that closes at the low is a supply fact, not a news fact, and no aggregator publishes it. The stock also printed sub-$1.00 closes on 08-19, 08-20, 08-21 and 09-01, putting it inside the Nasdaq $1.00 minimum-bid window with a results print as the next catalyst - if the market were discounting a forced compliance action the stock would not have been bid +14% pre-market on a rebrand.
